import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G

gi,go=G['Demo pair 1 input'],G['Demo pair 1 output']
# connected components of each color; find which became 4. Try bounding boxes: maybe 4 = fill rectangles of one color that form large solid blocks? Check: cells with value v where a filled rect... Find the changed regions.
changed={(i,j) for i in range(30) for j in range(30) if gi[i][j]!=go[i][j]}
ys=[i for i,_ in changed]; xs=[j for _,j in changed]
print(min(ys),max(ys),min(xs),max(xs))
# print mask
for i in range(30):
    print(''.join('#' if (i,j) in changed else '.' for j in range(30)))

steps.text:
Changed cells: 3x7 rectangles of color 8 (rows2-7 cols4-9, rows12-16 cols22-26, rows17-22 cols10-16). In demo input those are all 8s. So rule: fill with 4 any solid rectangle? All 8-regions changed; other 8-regions didn't. The unchanged 8 components were scattered (size ≤5), changed ones were 7x7 blocks? Actually 7 rows x 7 cols = 49 cells but each region shows 7x7=49 (#). Wait first block rows2-7 cols4-9 is 6x7=42. Hmm counts: 43+... maybe the actual rectangles in output replace entire bounding box? Let's check what input value at edges — mask shows full rects of #. Maybe rule: find largest solid rectangle of a single color and fill it with 4? Changed regions: values 8 in both cases. Other 8 components are noise. But there was a "1" component of size 55... check if that became 4? No—changed only 145 cells.

Better: identify connected components of value v whose bounding box fully filled with same value AND area > threshold → fill with 4. Unchanged 8-components: sizes 4,3,4... small. 7x7-ish. Test on test grid.

Let me verify precisely which input rectangles: for each comp, bbox must be entirely that color. Check.

    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); ch={(y,x) for y in range(H) for x in range(W) if g[y][x]!=go[y][x]}
    seen=set(); ncomps=[]
    for p in sorted(ch):
        if p in seen: continue
        q=deque([p]); cs=[p]; seen.add(p)
        while q:
            y,x=q.popleft()
            for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                n=(y+dy,x+dx)
                if n in ch and n not in seen: seen.add(n); q.append(n); cs.append(n)
        ncomps.append(cs)
    for c in ncomps:
        ys=[y for y,_ in c]; xs=[x for _,x in c]
        r0,r1=min(ys),max(ys); c0,c1=min(xs),max(xs)
        # is each comp a full solid rectangle of ONE color?
        col=g[r0][c0]
        ok=all(g[y][x]==col for y in range(r0,r1+1) for x in range(c0,c1+1))
        # is this bbox a maximal solid rect?
        ext=False
        if r0>0 and all(g[r0-1][x]==col for x in range(c0,c1+1)): ext=True
        if c0>0 and all(g[y][c0-1]==col for y in range(r0,r1+1)): ext=True
        if r1<H-1 and all(g[r1+1][x]==col for x in range(c0,c1+1)): ext=True
        if c1<W-1 and all(g[y][c1+1]==col for y in range(r0,r1+1)): ext=True
        print('comp',(r0,c0,r1,c1),'color',col,'area',(r1-r0+1)*(c1-c0+1),'full',ok,'maximal',not ext)

def maximal_rects(g,col):
    hh=len(g);ww=len(g[0]);out=[]
    for i in range(hh):
        for j in range(ww):
            if g[i][j]!=col: continue
            h=1
            while i+h<hh and g[i+h][j]==col: h+=1
            for hh2 in range(1,h+1):
                w=1
                while j+w<ww and all(g[r][j+w]==col for r in range(i,i+hh2)): w+=1
                if hh2<2 or w<2: continue
                up = i>0 and all(g[r][j]==col for r in range(i-1,i+hh2))
                lf = j>0 and all(g[r][j-1]==col for r in range(i,i+hh2))
                if up or lf: continue
                out.append((i,j,hh2,w))
    return out

def maximal_rects(g,col):
    hh=len(g);ww=len(g[0]);out=[]
    for i in range(hh):
        for j in range(ww):
            if g[i][j]!=col: continue

            for hh2 in range(1,h+1):

def is_maximal(m,g,col):

    hh=len(g);ww=len(g[0]);out=[]
